item.text:
## Audit findings

### 1. Axiom versus Serre II §2 Prop. 3

> `axiom AX_integralClosure_dvr (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] ... :
> IsDiscreteValuationRing (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L)`

**Classification: faithful specialization of the DVR clause.**

Every substantive hypothesis required by the cited result is present or follows from the specialization:

- `p : ℕ` with `[Fact p.Prime]` makes `ℤ_[p]` the ring of \(p\)-adic integers and `ℚ_[p]` the \(p\)-adic field.
- Mathlib supplies both `IsDiscreteValuationRing ℤ_[p]` and `IsFractionRing ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p]`; it also supplies the canonical algebra structure. Thus \(A=\mathbb Z_p\) is a DVR with fraction field \(K=\mathbb Q_p\). [Mathlib’s \(p\)-adic-integer documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/PadicIntegers.html)
- The missing source assumption that \(A\) or \(K\) is complete is not missing mathematically: completeness is built into the concrete choice \(\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Q_p\), rather than passed as an axiom argument.
- `[Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[p] L]` makes \(L/K\) a field extension. A field algebra map is injective.
- `[FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] L]` says exactly that \([L:K]<\infty\).
- `[Algebra ℤ_[p] L] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] L]` pins the `ℤ_[p] → L` map to the composite through `ℚ_[p]`. Mathlib explicitly proves `IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq`; the tower is more than an informal compatibility condition. [Mathlib algebra-tower documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Tower.html)
- `integralClosure ℤ_[p] L` is precisely the subring/subalgebra of elements of \(L\) integral over the supplied image of \(\mathbb Z_p\).
- Mathlib defines `IsDiscreteValuationRing` as a local PID that is not a field and notes its equivalence with Serre’s “PID with a unique nonzero prime ideal” formulation. Thus the Lean conclusion is not stronger than the ordinary DVR conclusion. [Mathlib DVR definition](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/DiscreteValuationRing/Basic.html)

The cited mathematical clause is independently described in the literature as: for a complete discretely valued \(K\), finite \(L/K\), and \(B\) the integral closure of its valuation ring, \(B\) is a DVR and is free of rank \([L:K]\). [Serre citation cross-reference](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-56694-4_13), [independent statement](https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~ajs1005/ANT/notes_s3-4.pdf)

The axiom asserts only the first clause. It does not assert freeness, rank, completeness, valuation uniqueness, ramification formulas, or lying-over.

### 2. Separability and finiteness

**Classification: no hidden strengthening.**

There is no missing finiteness hypothesis: it is exactly `[FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] L]`.

If one reads a version of the cited theorem formulated for finite separable extensions, the absence of an explicit separability argument is harmless here. Every finite extension of \(\mathbb Q_p\) is separable because \(\mathbb Q_p\) has characteristic zero. Hence the Lean hypotheses imply separability mathematically.

No Galois, normality, residue-field finiteness, or tame-ramification hypothesis is needed for the DVR conclusion.

### 3. Arbitrary algebra structures and the scope caveat

> “the quantification over arbitrary `Algebra ℚ_[p] L` structure maps φ is harmless”

**Classification: substantively correct.**

For every chosen field embedding
\[
\varphi:\mathbb Q_p\hookrightarrow L,
\]
the tower condition makes the `ℤ_[p] → L` structure map the restriction/composite
\[
\mathbb Z_p\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p\xrightarrow{\varphi}L.
\]
The image \(\varphi(\mathbb Z_p)\) is isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z_p\), is a complete DVR under the transported valuation or ideal-adic topology, and has fraction field \(\varphi(\mathbb Q_p)\). Also \(L\) is finite over that image field. Serre therefore applies separately to every such embedding.

There is no requirement that \(\varphi\) already be continuous for some independently chosen topology on \(L\): the axiom supplies no topology or valuation on \(L\), and Serre constructs/transports the relevant one from the embedded base field.

However, this sentence is too strong:

> “every instance is **literally** Prop. 3 at `(A, K, L) = (φ(ℤ_[p]), φ(ℚ_[p]), L)`”

**Classification: wording caveat.**

It is not literally or definitionally the same Lean object. `integralClosure ℤ_[p] L` is formed using the abstract base type `ℤ_[p]`, whereas the closure of `φ(ℤ_[p])` uses an image subring. They have the same carrier in \(L\), or at minimum are canonically ring-equivalent, after using the tower equality and invariance of integrality under the base-ring isomorphism. DVR-ness then transports across that equivalence.

Recommended replacement:

> “Every instance is an isomorphic transport of Proposition 3 applied to the embedded pair \(\varphi(\mathbb Z_p)\subseteq\varphi(\mathbb Q_p)\subseteq L\).”

Likewise:

> “`integralClosure ℤ_[p] L` depends only on the image subring `φ(ℤ_[p])`”

is mathematically correct at the level of its carrier and ring isomorphism class, but should not be read as a claim of definitional equality between differently typed subrings.

### 4. Citation synopsis caveat

> “the valuation of `B` is the unique extension of that of `A`”

**Classification: normalization/attribution caveat, irrelevant to this axiom.**

This needs careful phrasing. The unique extension is canonically an absolute value, valuation topology, or equivalence class of valuations. For normalized integer-valued valuations one generally has
\[
v_L|_K=e\,v_K
\]
in a ramified extension, not literal equality. An independent formulation says there is a unique valuation on \(L\) inducing the base topology. Since the axiom does not assert any valuation-extension clause, this imprecision does not make the axiom stronger.

It would also be safer not to insist that every item in the long synopsis—especially uniqueness—is contained in Proposition 3 itself unless checked against the cited edition. The DVR clause and finite-free/completeness clauses are securely associated with the proposition.

### 5. Minor quantifier caveat

> `(L : Type)`

**Classification: harmless weakening.**

This quantifies only over universe-0 types, rather than `(L : Type*)` at an arbitrary universe. That makes the Lean axiom formally narrower than the unrestricted mathematical theorem, never stronger. It does not affect ordinary finite extensions used by the consumers.

## Bottom line

The axiom itself states exactly the DVR clause of Serre’s theorem specialized to \((\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Q_p)\). It does not omit a necessary finiteness or separability condition, and the scalar-tower argument successfully prevents an unrelated `ℤ_[p]`-algebra structure.

The faithfulness entry is mathematically sound but should replace “literally” with “canonically equivalent/by transport” and qualify the “unique extension of the valuation” synopsis.

**VERDICT: FAITHFUL-WITH-CAVEATS**
